speaker: Doctor
text: I need to clarify your symptoms first; have you noticed any unusual movements, tremors, or changes in your speech patterns recently? Additionally, have you experienced increased thirst or frequent urination alongside the weight gain?

speaker: Patient
text: 55-year-old male. The patient has demonstrated inappropriate behavior, including making unfitting comments and attempts to kiss strangers, over the past 6 months. He shows disinterest in family interactions and has developed a particular craving for chocolate pudding and potato chips, resulting in a 10 kg weight gain. The patient also presents as unkempt.

speaker: Doctor
text: Has this inappropriate behavior and weight gain been present all the time, or did it develop gradually over the past 6 months? REQUEST TEST: Fasting Glucose and HbA1c. REQUEST IMAGES: Brain_MRI.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Inappropriate behavior. I also have Disinterest in family interactions, Craving for specific foods, Significant weight gain, Apathy, Blunted affect.

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No significant medical history provided. Social history: No detailed social history provided; recent behavior includes attempting to initiate inappropriate physical contact with strangers.

speaker: Patient
text: The patient avoids questions and instead comments on unrelated subjects. Shows apathy towards surroundings and interactions. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Migraine and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text: That is not correct; migraines do not cause inappropriate sexual behavior, severe apathy, or rapid weight gain from food cravings. I need to know if you have noticed any changes in your memory, such as forgetting recent conversations or getting lost in familiar places. Also, have you noticed your vision becoming blurry or any new headaches? REQUEST TEST: TSH and Free T4. REQUEST TEST: Prolactin.

speaker: Doctor
text: Since your fasting glucose, HbA1c, thyroid levels, and prolactin are all normal, can you confirm if you have experienced any recent head trauma, or if your behavior has become specifically more focused on sexual topics or rituals? DIAGNOSIS READY: Frontal Lobe Dementia (specifically behavioral variant Frontotemporal Dementia).
